One error, Three systems and Closed loop.

⚠️ D12 VISA ALERT: The rules have changed.

If you’re in Indonesia on a Pre-Investment (D12) Visa, onshore extension is no longer allowed. To remain compliant, offshore application is now mandatory.

🚨 Important rules to remember:

- Once you are approaching or have entered 180 days of stay, you must exit Indonesia.
- ⁠To obtain another 180 days, you simply re-enter Indonesia, as long as your multiple-entry D12 visa is still active.
- ⁠If you exit Indonesia before reaching 180 days, that is not a problem — you may re-enter anytime using the same active multiple entry D12 visa.

⚠️ Extra caution: If your multiple-entry status has expired, you must leave Indonesia immediately, in accordance with your remaining stay permit validity.

Always check your e-visa, multiple entry status, and stay permit. If your dates are approaching, book your flight early and plan your next move.

Does Bali have legal authority to impose entry requirements?
